content.intro: Learn cross-site scripting (xss) through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines cross-site scripting (xss) as part of security and privacy. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Reflected and stored XSS; Template autoescaping; Safe HTML handling; Content sanitization; Security implications of rich-text content. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Reflected and stored XSS
items.text: Reflected and stored XSS is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

items.title: Template autoescaping
items.text: An API contract specifies resources, methods, body validation, authentication, permissions, status codes, pagination, versioning and error formats. JSON transport alone does not make an API safe or complete.

items.title: Safe HTML handling
items.text: Safe HTML handling is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

items.title: Content sanitization
items.text: For Content sanitization, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
